CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Isukuti is a lively drum dance of the (1 mark)
   A. Somali
   B. Maasai
   C. Turkana
   D. Luhya

2. What is the job of the hollow shell of a drum? (1 mark)
   A. To make the sound fuller and louder
   B. To tie the ropes
   C. To hold the beater
   D. To keep the skin wet

3. If you tighten the skin of a drum, the sound becomes (1 mark)
   A. lower
   B. silent
   C. softer for ever
   D. higher

4. Smudging a charcoal drawing means (1 mark)
   A. erasing it completely
   B. folding the paper
   C. rubbing it gently so the tones blend
   D. painting over it

5. Which position takes the centre pass to start the game? (1 mark)
   A. GS
   B. C, Centre
   C. GD
   D. GK

6. The basic knot for the macramé ball is the (1 mark)
   A. sailor's knot
   B. reef knot
   C. fisherman's bend
   D. overhand knot

7. A lighter tone of a colour is called a (1 mark)
   A. primary
   B. shade
   C. outline
   D. tint

8. Why should your composed rhythm be your own idea? (1 mark)
   A. To be different from the teacher only
   B. To finish faster
   C. To use more paper
   D. Original work shows honesty

9. The Kodaly hand sign for r is (1 mark)
   A. a flat hand held level
   B. a sloping palm
   C. a closed fist
   D. a wave

10. Which nationality was Zoltan Kodaly, whose method uses hand signs? (1 mark)
   A. Hungarian
   B. Chinese
   C. Brazilian
   D. Kenyan

11. On the Kenyan flag, red stands for (1 mark)
   A. the land
   B. the blood shed in the struggle for freedom
   C. the sky
   D. peace

12. Compared with the medium start, the elongated start has the back knee (1 mark)
   A. in the air
   B. further forward
   C. further back
   D. on the line

13. In a medium start, the rear knee is level with (1 mark)
   A. the start line
   B. the heel of the front foot
   C. the middle of the front foot
   D. the toe of the back foot

14. Which is a safe surface for gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Concrete
   B. A mat or soft clean ground
   C. Wet tiles
   D. A stony floor

15. A sequence in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   B. a rule break
   C. a single balance
   D. a type of mat

16. What is a spotter or supporting partner's job? (1 mark)
   A. To laugh
   B. To leave
   C. To help gently as your teacher shows you
   D. To push you

17. At a wedding, we are most likely to hear (1 mark)
   A. topical songs only
   B. marriage songs
   C. work songs only
   D. funeral songs

18. A folk song is (1 mark)
   A. a traditional song belonging to a community
   B. a computer song
   C. a song only for cities
   D. a song without a message

19. A song that is played fast has a (1 mark)
   A. soft dynamic
   B. long title
   C. low pitch
   D. fast tempo

20. After taking photos, choosing the best ones is called (1 mark)
   A. selecting
   B. painting
   C. smudging
   D. hiding

21. Early morning and late afternoon light is (1 mark)
   A. harsh
   B. absent
   C. soft and gentle
   D. too dark always

22. Which light is best for outdoor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Only midday shadows
   B. A torch in the eyes
   C. Darkness
   D. Natural sunlight falling on the subject

23. Which note is played with the thumb hole and hole 1 covered? (1 mark)
   A. G
   B. B
   C. A
   D. C

24. Tonguing means (1 mark)
   A. chewing
   B. rolling on the floor
   C. singing loudly
   D. saying too or doo quietly at the start of each note

25. Which hand is at the top of the recorder? (1 mark)
   A. Left
   B. Neither
   C. Both feet
   D. Right

26. The bottom part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. head joint
   B. thumb hole
   C. foot joint
   D. beak

27. Music is written on a (1 mark)
   A. table
   B. wall
   C. staff
   D. ruler

28. Why should you not dive into shallow water? (1 mark)
   A. It makes noise
   B. It makes splashes
   C. It looks silly
   D. You can hit the bottom and hurt your head or neck

29. Prone means (1 mark)
   A. standing
   B. face down
   C. face up
   D. sitting

30. How does the hawk tag? (1 mark)
   A. By pushing
   B. Gently on the back or shoulders
   C. By pulling clothes
   D. By tripping

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how animal games help to keep the body healthy. (4 marks)

32. Describe how to compose a short melody with d, r and m, and how to check that it is a good melody. (5 marks)

33. State the lengths of a crotchet rest and a quaver rest and how to show a rest when clapping. (3 marks)

34. Compose a four-beat rhythmic pattern using a crotchet, a pair of quavers and a rest, and write it in rhythm names. (4 marks)

35. Give three hygiene rules for the pool. (3 marks)

36. Explain the difference between the prone float and the supine float. (3 marks)

37. State four rules of netball. (4 marks)

38. Explain why netball is called a team game. (2 marks)

39. State the length of a crotchet and of a quaver in beats. (2 marks)

40. What does giving with the ball mean in netball catching? (2 marks)

41. What does singing in unison mean? Why is it good for an anthem? (3 marks)

42. Explain the difference between a sacred song and a patriotic song. (3 marks)

43. Why are funeral songs usually slow and sad? (3 marks)

44. Write a melody that goes up by steps from d to m and comes down to d, and state the number of notes. (3 marks)

45. Why should you delete poor photographs from a device? (3 marks)

46. Why is it important not to share a recorder before cleaning it? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Luhya
   Isukuti is played by the Luhya people, especially the Isukha and Idakho.

2. A — To make the sound fuller and louder
   The air inside the hollow body makes the sound louder.

3. D — higher
   A tighter skin vibrates faster and gives a higher sound.

4. C — rubbing it gently so the tones blend
   Smudging spreads the charcoal so that light and dark blend smoothly.

5. B — C, Centre
   The Centre takes the centre pass.

6. D — overhand knot
   The learner uses overhand knots to make the net around the core.

7. D — tint
   Adding white makes a tint.

8. D — Original work shows honesty
   Creating your own pattern shows integrity.

9. B — a sloping palm
   Ray is a palm that slopes upward.

10. A — Hungarian
   Zoltan Kodaly was a Hungarian music teacher.

11. B — the blood shed in the struggle for freedom
   Red stands for the blood shed for freedom.

12. C — further back
   Elongated means longer, so the feet are further apart.

13. C — the middle of the front foot
   The medium start places the rear knee by the middle of the front foot.

14. B — A mat or soft clean ground
   Soft, flat surfaces prevent injuries.

15. A — a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   A sequence links skills one after the other.

16. C — To help gently as your teacher shows you
   A partner supports carefully and only in the way taught.

17. B — marriage songs
   Marriage songs praise the couple and give good wishes.

18. A — a traditional song belonging to a community
   Folk songs are passed on by singing.

19. D — fast tempo
   Tempo is speed.

20. A — selecting
   Selecting means choosing the best.

21. C — soft and gentle
   These times give soft light.

22. D — Natural sunlight falling on the subject
   Natural light is best.

23. B — B
   B uses the thumb and the first hole.

24. D — saying too or doo quietly at the start of each note
   Tonguing separates notes clearly.

25. A — Left
   The left hand is at the top and the right hand at the bottom.

26. C — foot joint
   The foot joint ends in the bell.

27. C — staff
   The staff has five lines and four spaces.

28. D — You can hit the bottom and hurt your head or neck
   Shallow water is dangerous for diving.

29. B — face down
   Prone is face down.

30. B — Gently on the back or shoulders
   Gentle tagging keeps everyone safe.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: They strengthen muscles, stretch the body, improve balance and coordination and make the heart and lungs stronger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give each note a syllable, using steps. End on d. Sing it with hand signs. Check that it has variation and stepwise motion and that it ends on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five valid points.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet rest is one beat of silence and a quaver rest is half a beat of silence. When clapping, we do not clap but keep the beat silently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each length, 1 mark for showing the rest.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example taa ta-te (rest) taa. Any four-beat pattern with all three parts and ending on a crotchet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four beats, 1 mark for using all three, 1 mark for correct names, 1 mark for ending on a long note.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Shower before and after; do not spit or pass urine in the pool; do not drink the water; dry yourself and change into dry clothes. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prone is face down in the water with arms stretched forward. Supine is on the back with the face up and ears in the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each float, 1 mark for the difference.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: No running with the ball; pass or shoot within three seconds; no contact; defenders stand 0.9 metres away; start with a centre pass. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Players must pass to each other to move the ball and score. No player can run with the ball alone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for passing or cooperation, 1 mark for the explanation.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: A crotchet is one beat and a quaver is half a beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Bending the arms as the ball arrives so as to take the force out of it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bending arms, 1 mark for softening the catch.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone sings the same notes at the same time. It is simple and everybody can join in together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A sacred song is a song of worship that praises God. A patriotic song shows love for the country, such as the national anthem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for an example.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: They comfort the family and remember the person who has died, so the mood is calm and serious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: d r m r d. There are five notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for going up, 1 mark for coming down, 1 mark for five.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: To save memory space, keep only good pictures and make it easier to find the best ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Germs from the mouth can spread illnesses such as colds through the mouthpiece.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for the mouth or mouthpiece, 1 mark for spreading illness.
